name: @es-plus/mcp-server

tools.name: detect_project_target
tools.description: Detect which es-plus target (vue3 / vue2 / antdv) matches the user's project, given the project's package.json content. The MCP client (e.g. Claude Code) reads the file from the workspace and passes it here. Use this BEFORE calling generate_scene / generate_composition / generate_crud / generate_form / generate_table / generate_dialog (or the legacy generate_crud_page / generate_crud_schema) / get_component_api so you pick the right target instead of defaulting to vue3.

packageJson.description: Raw string content of the user project's package.json. Read it with your file-read tool (e.g. read_file) and pass the full JSON text here.

tools.name: generate_scene
tools.description: FRONT DOOR — SCENE ROUTER: the scene-first way to generate es-plus code. Call with `scene` = what the user is building ('crud' page / standalone 'table' / standalone 'form' / 'dialog') and `intent` = that scene's intent table. For scene='crud' the intent is exactly the generate_crud argument object (name, apiUrl, surfaces — your one reasoning step is still filling `surfaces`); for the fragment scenes it is exactly the generate_table / generate_form / generate_dialog argument object. Routing and emission are deterministic, and the output is byte-identical to the corresponding legacy tool. When the client supports MCP structured output, the artifact envelope (`contract` / `files` / `config` / `warnings` / `fingerprint`) is also returned as `structuredContent`; the text content is unchanged. Use generate_composition when several of these pieces must live TOGETHER in one page; `generate_crud` remains available as the compatibility entry for a plain list/table page and produces the same bytes as scene='crud'.

scene.description: Which artifact the user wants: 'crud' (a full page with a table — the composite case), 'table' (one standalone es-table), 'form' (one standalone es-form), 'dialog' (one reusable add/edit dialog). Pick by WHAT is being built, not by which tool name you remember.

intent.description: The scene's intent table. scene='crud': the same keys as the generate_crud compat entry (name/apiUrl/surfaces/…). scene='table'|'form'|'dialog': the same keys as generate_table/generate_form/generate_dialog (fields/…). Fill only the keys for the chosen scene; unknown keys are rejected with a did-you-mean.

tools.name: generate_composition
tools.description: PAGE COMPOSER — assemble several standalone fragments into ONE working page (Page.vue + one file per node). Give it 1+ nodes, each `{ id, role?, scene, intent }` where scene is 'table' / 'form' / 'dialog' (at most one form; tables and dialogs may repeat) and intent is exactly that scene's standalone tool argument. The wiring is derived deterministically from the artifact runtime contract: a row button whose key equals a dialog node id opens that dialog (title from the dialog intent's defaultTitle); the query form reloads the default table from page 1; reset reloads it with cleared filters; submit becomes a page event 'save'; a successful dialog submit refreshes the default table. The form fragment only emits the events its `buttons` render — `buttons` defaults to 'none' (no buttons at all: query/submit/reset never fire), 'query' emits query+reset, 'submit' emits submit+reset. Composition does NOT rewrite a node's intent, so wires from a channel that form cannot emit are reported in `warnings` (they would never fire — e.g. page 'save' with no save button). The default table is the node with role 'master', else the only table; in a multi-table page with neither, data channels become page events instead of guessing (and the artifact/envelope warnings name the upgrade and both remedies: the page's per-node `<nodeCamel>Refresh`/`<nodeCamel>Reload` methods — node `order-list` exposes `orderListRefresh`/`orderListReload` — or declare role 'master'). Pass `wires` to declare master-detail style links yourself (e.g. master row-action key 'view' → detail table reload, where the row is passed as the model; use to.model to pass only chosen row fields); an explicit wire overrides the derived one for the same source. Wire targets must be callable by the generated page: table refresh/reload, form validate/resetFields, component-dialog open/close; `open` is only reachable from a row-action (it carries the row), and a row-action key must match a declared rowButtons key. `behavior: 'ui-only'` wires only the UI (row button → dialog open) and turns query/reset/success into page events so the host performs its own requests; the default `data-wiring` only derives table reload/refresh (no HTTP requests — use scene 'crud' for built-in add/edit/delete). Use this when the user wants these pieces TOGETHER in one page but the request is not a CRUD page (use generate_scene/generate_crud for 'crud'). The page exposes refresh/reload/open and emits row-action/save (+ query/reset/success when there is no default table or behavior is ui-only). When the client supports MCP structured output, the composition envelope (nodes/wires/faces/page/fingerprint) is also returned as `structuredContent`; the text content is unchanged.

name.description: Display name for the composed page (summary only). The component name is always ComposedPage.

target.description: Page target. Defaults to the first node's explicit target, then vue3. All nodes must share one target.

behavior.description: Data-wiring mode (default 'data-wiring'). 'data-wiring' derives query/reset → default table reload and dialog onSuccess → default table refresh; it does NOT generate HTTP requests (fragment intents carry no apiUrl/actions) — use scene 'crud' for built-in add/edit/delete requests. 'ui-only' wires only the UI (row button → dialog open) and turns query/reset/success into page events so the host performs requests itself. Explicit wires apply in both modes.

id.description: Node id in kebab-case (e.g. 'users', 'query-form', 'edit'). It is the output file name (<id>.vue), the template ref source, and — for a dialog node — the row-button key that opens it ('edit' binds the 编辑 button).

role.description: Optional role label (kebab-case, unique per scene). `master` marks the table that form query/reset and dialog success default to in a multi-table page. Which row button loads a detail table is a product decision — express it in `wires`, not as a role.

scene.description: Which standalone fragment this node is. 'crud' is not composable (it is already a full page).

intent.description: The node's intent table: exactly the generate_table / generate_form / generate_dialog argument object for this scene. For a dialog, `defaultTitle` is the title used by the composed page's open().

nodes.description: The page's nodes: at most one 'form'; 'table' and 'dialog' may repeat (master-detail, multi-dialog). A row button whose key equals a dialog node id opens that dialog.

channel.description: Source channel declared by ARTIFACT_RUNTIME: row-action / submit / query / reset / onSuccess.

Target channel the composed page can CALL (ARTIFACT_RUNTIME.invokable): table refresh/reload, form validate/resetFields, component-dialog open/close. `model` is data, not a method. A composable dialog (mode 'composable') has no template ref — only a row-action may open it. `open` requires a row, so it is only accepted from a row-action source.

model.description: Row → reload params mapping, only for a row-action source targeting `reload`. Values are single-level row fields written as '$row.<field>' (e.g. { departmentId: '$row.departmentId' } → reload({ departmentId: row.departmentId })). Omit to pass the whole row (reload(row)).

event.description: Page event name to emit (becomes part of the page's emits face).

when.description: Required for row-action sources: the button key this wire applies to. It must match a rowButtons key declared in the source table's intent — an undeclared key would generate a branch that never fires.

wires.description: Explicit wiring, validated against the same runtime contract as derived wiring. An explicit wire overrides the derived wire for the same source (node + channel + rowAction key). Row-action targets receive the clicked row by default (e.g. master row → detail table reload(row)); set `to.model` to pass only chosen fields (e.g. { departmentId: '$row.departmentId' }) instead of the whole row.

tools.name: generate_crud
tools.description: COMPAT ENTRY (adapter) — same product as generate_scene with scene='crud' (byte-identical), kept for hosts that already call this name. Use it for ANY request that involves a list/table, CRUD, search + results, or multiple es-plus pieces working together. Your ONE job is to fill `surfaces`: set query/table/form field lists and the dialog list to match what the request implies (any subset is valid — table-only, query+table, table+add/edit, full CRUD, etc.). A `surfaces.dialog` entry is either a canned key ('add'/'edit'/'view') or a full object `{ key, title?, width?, fullscreen?, formItems? }` when the request names a custom dialog id/title/width or a per-dialog field list. Routing is then deterministic: table-bearing requests compile through the golden-covered single generator; no-table subsets emit self-contained fragments. Do NOT manually orchestrate generate_form/generate_table/generate_dialog for a composite page — fill surfaces here and let the routing compose them. When the user wants several standalone pieces assembled into one page (not a CRUD page), call generate_composition instead. Use the standalone tools only for an explicit single-component ask or to embed a fragment next to non-es-plus components. Optional config knobs — tableOptions / formLayout / operationColumn / tableBtns / toolbarBtns / expandConfig / treeConfig / mergeConfig — may be set alongside `surfaces`; each is forwarded verbatim into the composed config, so fill them only when the request names those specifics. A no-table request whose only surface is `dialog` emits one JSX composable PER dialog entry (named use<Key>Dialog): each entry's `formItems` overrides the shared form/query body, its `title` becomes open()'s default title, and its `width`/`fullscreen` are applied. Because the dialog body is a JSX render, that path needs a JSX plugin; if the host wants a self-contained dialog with NO JSX dependency, call generate_dialog with mode:'component' instead. When the client supports MCP structured output, the artifact envelope is also returned as `structuredContent`; the text content is unchanged.

apiUrl.description: REST base URL for this resource, e.g. "/api/users"

prop.description: Field key in the data model (camelCase), e.g. "userName"

labelKey.description: i18n label key for this field (takes precedence over `label`; only takes effect once the host entry assembles the plugin with a `t` option).

formtype.description: Pick by the field's MEANING, not by keyword: status/type/enum/gender → Select; date/time → DatePicker/TimePicker; image/avatar/file → Upload; long text → Input (attrs.type:'textarea'); on/off → Switch; multi-choice → Checkbox; tree → Cascader; score → Rate; numeric value (amount/price/quantity/stock/count/money/integer) → InputNumber. Default Input.

querySpan.description: Grid width of this field in the query form (1-24; 2 columns = 12 each). Column count is set PER FIELD — there is no layout-level span key.

formSpan.description: Grid width of this field in the add/edit form (1-24; 2 columns = 12 each). Column count is set PER FIELD — there is no layout-level span key.

required.description: Enforce a value with this rule (same effect as field-level `required`; prefer the field-level key for unconditional requirements).

pattern.description: RegExp SOURCE STRING the value must match (e.g. "^1\d{10}$"), not a RegExp object.

min.description: Minimum length for strings / minimum value for numbers.

max.description: Maximum length for strings / maximum value for numbers.

type.description: Value type validated by this rule.

message.description: Message shown when the rule fails — REQUIRED, write it in the user's language.

trigger.description: 'blur' validates when the field loses focus; 'change' validates while the value changes.

rules.description: Validation rules for this field. Use `pattern`/`min`/`max`/`type` for format constraints and `trigger` for when validation runs; `message` is REQUIRED. A rule carrying `type` is dispatched ONLY to that type validator (async-validator `getValidationMethod`) — a `pattern` on the SAME rule is silently ignored, so when the user states BOTH a regex and a type, emit them as TWO separate rules. For a plain text length cap (e.g. '最多 20 字') prefer `attrs.maxlength`; a `min`/`max` rule validates values with a message but does not block typing. Emit these rather than dropping a format/range requirement the user stated.

attrs.description: Extra component props, e.g. { type: 'textarea', maxlength: 200 }

apiParams.description: Remote options source for Select/Cascader — use instead of dataOptions when options come from an API.

formatter.description: Extension point: a JS arrow-function source string for read-only cell formatting, e.g. "(row) => row.amount.toFixed(2)".

render.description: Extension point: a render-function source string for a fully custom cell/control.

isHidden.description: Conditional visibility (AI-06): PLAIN JSON data, never a JS function string. Semantics: the field is HIDDEN while the condition HOLDS (`{ field: 'payType', op: 'eq', value: 'cash' }` = hidden while payType is cash). TWO forms, never mixed within one node: (1) legacy condition `{ field, op?, value? }` — `op` is ONE of eq | ne | in | nIn | empty | notEmpty | truthy | falsy (default eq); preferred for simple comparisons; (2) JSONLogic-shaped expression node for ordering / OR / nesting, e.g. `{ '>': [{ var: 'amount' }, 100] }` or `{ or: [...] }` — expression ops (closed set): var == != > >= < <= in nin empty notEmpty truthy falsy and or not if. An expression op such as `>` or `!=` inside a legacy `{field, op, value}` node is INVALID (the runtime warns and treats the field as visible) — use form (2) for those. An ARRAY of nodes is AND (hidden only when ALL hold) and may mix both forms. Applies to the query and add/edit forms, NOT the table column.

dependencies.description: Model paths that retrigger this rule. REQUIRED when `fulfill.value` is present.

when.description: Optional gate expression: the rule applies only while it evaluates truthy.

dataOptions.description: Literal option array for this field while the rule is active (NOT an expression — branch per case with one rule each).

required.description: Expression node evaluating to a boolean: make this field required.

disabled.description: Expression node evaluating to a boolean: disable this field.

value.description: Expression node evaluating to this field's new value, written back to the model (requires a non-empty `dependencies`).

reactions.description: Field linkage (AI-07): an array of {dependencies?, when?, fulfill} rules — PLAIN JSON, never JS callbacks. Use when THIS field's options/required/disabled/value depend on ANOTHER field (fulfill: {dataOptions?, required?, disabled?, value?}). `dependencies` lists the model paths that retrigger it (REQUIRED for fulfill.value). `when`, `fulfill.required`, `fulfill.disabled` and `fulfill.value` are JSONLogic EXPRESSION NODES only — e.g. `when: { '==': [{ var: 'country' }, 'us'] }`, `required: { '==': [{ var: 'country' }, 'us'] }` — never the `{ field, op, value }` condition form and never a bare boolean (those are for `isHidden`). `fulfill.dataOptions` is a literal option array, not an expression. One rule per case, LAST WINS. Applies to the query and add/edit forms, NOT the table column.

permissionValue.description: Permission CODE gating this field (RBAC, checked by the host's global permission(code)) — NOT a data-driven condition: use `isHidden` for show/hide by another field's value, `reactions` for options/required/disabled linkage.

query.description: Filter fields shown above the table

title.description: Dialog title (defaults to 新增/编辑/查看 for add/edit/view, else the key).

formItems.description: This dialog's own field list. When omitted: the `form` surface if present, else the `table` surface (table-bearing) or the `query` surface (no table).

anyOf.description: A full-parameter dialog — use when the request needs a custom id/title/width or a per-dialog field list.

dialog.description: Which dialogs the request needs: a canned key ("add"/"edit"/"view") or a full object { key, title?, width?, fullscreen?, formItems? }.

surfaces.description: The intent table — set only the surfaces the request implies. Any subset is valid.

target.description: Target renderer: vue3 (Element Plus), vue2 (Element UI), antdv (Ant Design Vue)

mode.description: Output mode for table-bearing results: 'schema' (schema.ts + wrapper SFC) or 'sfc' (single SFC)

actions.description: Explicit CRUD actions. If omitted, derived from surfaces.dialog / form presence.

heightType.description: 'height' = fixed height (value from `height`, or `tabHeight` if set); 'maxHeight' = capped at `tabHeight`; 'auto' = no container height constraint. Default 'auto'.

tabHeight.description: Height consumed for EVERY heightType: under 'height' it overrides `height`; under 'maxHeight' it is the cap.

height.description: Container height used ONLY when heightType is 'height' (ignored for 'auto'/'maxHeight' — use tabHeight there).

virtual.description: Enable virtual scrolling (vue3 el-table-v2; antdv a-table; vue2 degrades with a warning — use engine:'vxe' there).

editConfig.description: vxe inline editing (requires engine:'vxe' and a column-level `editRender`).

configTableOut.description: Map the LIST response onto table semantics when the backend shape differs from { rows, records, pageSize, pageNo }.

treeConfig.description: vxe-only rich tree config (distinct from the top-level cross-renderer `treeConfig`).

expandConfig.description: vxe-only row-expand switch (distinct from the top-level declarative `expandConfig`).

tableOptions.description: Table options, forwarded verbatim into the composed config's `tableOptions` block (border/stripe/rowkey/heightType/tabHeight/height/multiSelect/emptyText/size/defaultSort/leftText/engine/virtual/editConfig/configTableOut/tableOptions.treeConfig/tableOptions.expandConfig/…). The full key set and per-key semantics are the same as `StructuredCrudConfig.tableOptions`; unknown keys are rejected.

formLayout.description: Query form layout ({ labelWidth?, minFoldRows? }). Column count is PER FIELD via querySpan — formLayout has no span key; an unknown key is rejected.

operationColumn.description: Operation column config (`false` hides it): { label?, width?, fixed?, btns: [{ name, key?, type?, icon?, dialogKey?, confirm?, permissionValue? }] }.

tableBtns.description: Table toolbar buttons rendered above EsTable, e.g. [{ name: "导出", actionType: "export", position: "left" }]. Canonical keys are `name` + `actionType` + `position`; the legacy aliases `label`/`action` are accepted and normalized.

direction.description: Form-button direction (legacy form-side field; wins over 'position')

position.description: left | right (recommended positioning field; defaults to right)

toolbarBtns.description: Buttons rendered in the QUERY-FORM button area, appended after 查询/重置. No left/right placement here — when the description names a side, use `tableBtns` instead. Unknown keys are rejected.

expandConfig.description: Declarative row-expand content ({ title?, fields: [{prop, label?, labelKey?}] }) — the table gets ONE row-expander showing a read-only field list. Distinct from tableOptions.expandConfig (vxe-only switch). Unknown keys are rejected.

treeConfig.description: Declarative tree table ({ childrenField?, expandAll? }) — renders parent/child levels from each row's nested child array (row-key emitted automatically). Distinct from tableOptions.treeConfig (vxe-only). Unknown keys are rejected.

mergeConfig.description: Declarative row-merge ({ rowsBy: ['dept','team'] }) — merges those columns across consecutive rows with EQUAL values (the standard 'grouped rows' table). Cross-renderer (el-table / a-table / vxe). Unknown keys are rejected.

rowkey.description: Primary key for dialog PUT url / delete (default 'id')

An expression op inside a legacy {field, op, value} node is INVALID (runtime warns and treats the field as visible) — use form (2) for those. Applies to the query/filter form and the add/edit dialog forms, NOT the table column. Distinct from permissionValue (a permission code): use isHidden when visibility depends on another field's value.

dependencies.description: Model paths that retrigger this rule. REQUIRED when `fulfill.value` is present.

when.description: Optional gate expression: the rule applies only while it evaluates truthy. Must be a JSONLogic EXPRESSION NODE (e.g. { "==": [{ var: "country" }, "us"] }) — never the { field, op, value } legacy condition form (that belongs to isHidden), never a bare boolean. Plain JSON data, never a JS source string.

dataOptions.description: Literal option array for this field while the rule is active (NOT an expression — the DSL forbids object literals, so branch by declaring one rule per case with its own `when`).

required.description: Expression node evaluating to a boolean: make this field required.

disabled.description: Expression node evaluating to a boolean: disable this field.

value.description: Expression node evaluating to this field's new value, written back to the model (requires a non-empty `dependencies`).

reactions.description: Field-level linkage / computed rules (AI-07) — PLAIN JSON, never JS callbacks. Use when THIS field's options/required/disabled/value depend on ANOTHER field. Each rule `{ dependencies?, when?, fulfill }`: `dependencies` lists the model paths that retrigger it (REQUIRED for fulfill.value); `when` gates the rule; `fulfill` supplies `dataOptions` (literal array), `required`/`disabled` (boolean expressions) and/or `value` (this field's new value, written back). `when`/`required`/`disabled`/`value` are JSONLogic EXPRESSION NODES only (e.g. `{ '==': [{ var: 'country' }, 'us'] }`) — never the `{ field, op, value }` legacy condition form and never a bare boolean. Example: `city` options follow `province` → one rule per province with `when: { '==': [{ var: 'province' }, 'zj'] }` and `fulfill.dataOptions: [{label:'杭州',value:'hz'}]`. Applies to the query/filter form and add/edit dialog forms — NOT the table column.

fields.description: Field definitions — one per data attribute the user described

actions.description: Enabled CRUD actions inferred from the request: add/edit/delete/view/export/import

heightType.description: How the container height is applied: 'height' = fixed height (value from `height`, or `tabHeight` if set); 'maxHeight' = capped at `tabHeight` (a `height` value is IGNORED); 'auto' = no container height constraint. Default 'auto'.

tabHeight.description: Table height consumed for EVERY heightType: under 'height' it overrides `height`; under 'maxHeight' it is the cap. number → px, string → raw CSS value (e.g. '60vh'). Prefer it over `height` whenever a concrete height is needed — it is the only height key that applies when heightType is 'maxHeight'.

height.description: Container height used ONLY when heightType is 'height' (ignored for 'auto' / 'maxHeight' — use tabHeight there). Takes precedence over nothing: an explicit tabHeight always wins.

editConfig.description: Enable vxe inline editing (AI-09 子项④). vxe engine only — MUST be paired with tableOptions.engine:'vxe'. A cell is only editable when its column also declares `editRender`. An edit writes STRAIGHT into the row object of data-source (the host also gets update:dataSource); keepSource is auto-enabled only to keep a snapshot for revertData(). Listen to the cell-edit event ({ row, prop, value, oldValue }) to learn which cell changed and its previous value.

configTableOut.description: Map the LIST API response onto table semantics when the backend does not use the default flat shape { records, rows, pageSize, pageNo }. Each value is the FLAT response key (no deep paths). e.g. { list, count } → { tableData: 'list', total: 'count' }. Only the keys you set are remapped.

transform.description: Build the tree client-side from FLAT rows (needs rowField + parentField). vxe only.

rowField.description: Row id field for transform mode (default 'id').

parentField.description: Parent id field for transform mode (default 'parentId').

children.description: @deprecated vxe v4 alias of childrenField; normalized at runtime.

mapChildren.description: Field that caches original children in transform mode (default '_X_ROW_CHILD').

lazy.description: Lazy-load children (vxe only; the loader function itself is a Tier-3 extension point).

treeConfig.description: vxe-only rich tree config (the SAME-NAME top-level `treeConfig` is the cross-renderer narrow subset; when both are set the generator merges them into tableOptions.treeConfig with the top-level key winning).

accordion.description: Accordion mode: at most one row expanded at a time.

lazy.description: Lazy-load expand content (vxe only; the loader function itself is a Tier-3 extension point).

expandConfig.description: vxe-only row-expand switch (paired with `expand: true` / an expand column). Distinct from the top-level `expandConfig` (declarative read-only field list honored by all three renderers).

mode.description: Output mode: 'schema' (schema.ts + wrapper SFC) or 'sfc' (single self-contained SFC)

target.description: Target renderer: vue3 (Element Plus), vue2 (Element UI), antdv (Ant Design Vue)

direction.description: Form-button direction (legacy form-side field; wins over 'position')

position.description: left | right (recommended positioning field; defaults to right)

hasCustomRender.description: Declares the dialog body is hand-implemented in the wrapper SFC (a render function cannot travel in JSON). Relaxes the 'a mutating dialog needs formItems' check and emits a TODO(es-plus) marker; NOT forwarded to the dialog component.

isDraggable.description: Make the dialog draggable by its header.

maxHeight.description: Max height of the dialog body (scrolls beyond it).

showClose.description: Show the built-in close (X) entry; default true.

destroyOnClose.description: Destroy the dialog content on close (resets internal state each open).

closeOnClickModal.description: Close when the mask is clicked; default true.

closeOnPressEscape.description: Close when Escape is pressed; default true.

hiddenFullBtn.description: Hide the built-in fullscreen toggle button.

appendTo.description: CSS selector of the mount node (a DOM element cannot travel in JSON); the runtime resolves it with querySelector and falls back to document.body.

cacheKey.description: Instance cache key: repeat calls with the same key reuse one dialog instance (state survives close/reopen, recycled 10 min after close). Implemented identically by all three runtimes (vue3 / vue2 / ant-design-vue).

action.description: 'confirm' = validate the dialog form then run the submit path; 'cancel' = close + emit dialog-cancel; 'custom' (or omitted) = plain button the host wrapper must wire.

permissionValue.description: Permission code; filtered out unless the global permission function grants it.

configBtn.description: Declarative footer buttons. Omit to get the generated cancel+confirm pair. Each entry is JSON data — the click handler is attached by the runtime from `action`.

dialogs.description: Per-dialog configs keyed by dialog ID (add/edit/view/…). Declaring `dialogs` gives a dialog its own base keys (appearance/close behaviour, `configBtn`, `formItems`) and does NOT suppress button derivation — the toolbar and row-action buttons are still derived from `actions` unless `toolbarBtns`/`operationColumn` are declared explicitly (those two, never `dialogs`, hand the button surface over).

prop.description: Data key for this column, e.g. "userName". Omit for non-field columns (type: index/selection/expand).

label.description: Column header text. Omit for non-field columns.

labelKey.description: i18n key alternative to label (used when i18n is on)

type.description: Non-field column kind: 'index' = row number, 'selection' = checkbox column, 'expand' = row expander (needs an expandConfig/slot). Omit for a normal data column.

permissionValue.description: Permission code; the column is not rendered without it

groups.description: Nested child columns for a GROUP HEADER (multi-level). Recursive. Cross-renderer safe up to 2 levels (antdv supports N; vue3/vue2 default tables flatten beyond 1).

name.description: Inline-edit renderer name, e.g. '$input' | '$select' | '$textarea' | '$date' (vxe engine only).

type.description: 'default' = enter edit on trigger; 'visible' = editor always shown.

options.description: Option list for a '$select' editor (label/value pairs).

props.description: Props forwarded to the editor component.

editRender.description: Column-level inline editor (AI-09 子项④). vxe engine only — requires tableOptions.editConfig AND tableOptions.engine:'vxe'. Function-valued fields (events) and custom-registered renderers are out of scope (Tier-3).

title.description: Optional title shown at the top of the expanded row.

labelKey.description: i18n label key (used with a global t() function; takes precedence over `label`).

fields.description: Read-only fields rendered inside the expanded row, one per line as `label: value`.

expandConfig.description: Row-expand content declared ON the `type:'expand'` column (AI-09 子项②). Same shape/semantics as the top-level `expandConfig`; use it when the expander is not the leading column or when `columns` is the source of truth. If BOTH are set, the top-level one wins on the expand column. Distinct from `tableOptions.expandConfig` (the vxe `{accordion}` switch).

columns.description: Explicit table columns (escape hatch over the `fields`-derived columns). When present it REPLACES the derived data columns (override, not merge) — `fields` still drives the query/add/edit forms. Use it for multi-level group headers (`groups`), and non-field columns (`type`: index/selection/expand). The operation column is STILL appended from `actions`/`operationColumn` (set `operationColumn:false` to manage it yourself). Omit to keep the derived one-field-one-column behavior.

title.description: Optional title shown at the top of the expanded row.

labelKey.description: i18n label key (used with a global t() function; takes precedence over `label`).

fields.description: Read-only fields rendered inside the expanded row, one per line as `label: value`.

expandConfig.description: Row-expand content (AI-09 子项②). When set, the table gets ONE row-expander whose expanded content is a read-only field list. If `columns` already declares a `{type:'expand'}` column it is used as-is (position preserved) and the content attaches to it; otherwise the generator prepends a leading expand column. Distinct from `tableOptions.expandConfig` (the vxe `{accordion}` switch).

childrenField.description: Key name that holds a row's nested child nodes (default 'children'). Set only when the API nests children under a different key.

expandAll.description: Whether all nodes start expanded (default false).

treeConfig.description: Declarative tree table (AI-09 子项③). When set, the table renders parent/child levels from the nested child array in each row (row-key is emitted automatically). Static trees only — lazy/async loading is out of scope for this key. SAME NAME but DIFFERENT LAYER from `tableOptions.treeConfig` (the vxe-only VxeTreeConfig): this top-level key is the cross-renderer narrow subset, honored by el-table / a-table as well as vxe.

rowsBy.description: Column props to merge. Each is grouped by ADJACENT-EQUAL values: the first row of a run keeps the cell with rowspan = run length, the rest are merged away.

mergeConfig.description: Declarative row-merge (AI-23). `rowsBy: ['dept','team']` merges those columns across consecutive rows with equal values (the standard 'grouped rows' table). Cross-renderer narrow subset: el-table (span-method), a-table (per-column customCell) and vxe (mergeMethod) all honor it. The FUNCTIONAL escape hatch `tableOptions.spanMethod` remains Tier-3 and is NOT cross-renderer (a-table has no span-method channel) — if both are set, the explicit `spanMethod` wins.

tools.name: validate_config
tools.description: Validate an es-plus JSON configuration against its schema. Returns validation errors and fix suggestions. READ-ONLY: it judges and never repairs — format mistakes that the generators auto-fix (key aliases, relocated/nested keys, null placeholders, 'false'-style string booleans, dialog shorthands like dialogs:["add"]) are reported here as errors. Use this to inspect a config; the generator tools repair such mistakes before generating (they report each repair).

config.description: JSON string of the es-plus configuration to validate

type.description: Schema type to validate against. Available: api-params, btn-config, dialog-options, form-item, table-column, table-options, structured-crud-config (the input of generate_crud_from_config), es-table-config / es-form-config / es-dialog-config (the inputs of generate_table / generate_form / generate_dialog). Defaults to "form-item".

tools.name: list_form_types
tools.description: List all 14 available form field types (formtype) shared by es-plus on all three targets (vue3 / vue2 / antdv), with descriptions and usage examples.

tools.name: ingest_schema
tools.description: Pre-fill a structured CRUD config from an existing schema (OpenAPI JSON, JSON Schema, a sample JSON object, a TypeScript interface/type literal, or SQL CREATE TABLE DDL). Deterministic, no LLM: it maps each property's DATA TYPE to a formtype (integer→InputNumber, boolean→Switch, string+date→DatePicker, string+enum→Select, array+enum→Checkbox, else Input). For ts-interface, JSDoc becomes the label and non-optional members become required; for sql-ddl, COMMENT becomes the label and NOT NULL/PRIMARY KEY become required. Use this as a HEAD START, then review & edit the draft (narrow the query fields, add buttons/dialogs/permissions the schema can't express) and pass it to generate_crud_from_config. OpenAPI YAML is not supported in this version — convert to JSON first.

text.description: The schema source text (JSON for openapi/jsonSchema; a JSON object or array for sample-json; TypeScript interface/type source for ts-interface; CREATE TABLE DDL for sql-ddl).

name.description: Override the page name (PascalCase). Defaults to the schema title, else a placeholder.

apiUrl.description: Override the REST base URL, e.g. "/api/users". Defaults to a placeholder you must replace.

tools.name: refine_config
tools.description: Apply ONE round of refinement to a pinned CRUD config. The pin is just the StructuredCrudConfig JSON you (the host) already hold — there is no server-side session. YOU apply the user's natural-language correction to produce the `revised` config, then call this tool with the `previous` (last-pinned) and `revised` JSON. It deterministically (1) validates `revised` against the authoritative schema and (2) returns a structured DIFF of what this round changed — fields added/removed, formtype/membership changes, actions, AND changed top-level blocks (dialogs / formLayout / tableOptions / buttons / columns / permissions / generation options), so a round that only adds an edit dialog or widens the form is not reported as "no change". If `revised` is invalid, you get the schema errors instead of a diff — fix and retry. Pass `revised` to generate_crud_from_config once you're happy. This tool does NOT call a model; the reasoning is yours.

previous.description: JSON string of the previously pinned config (omit for the first round).

revised.description: JSON string of the config after you applied the user's correction.

tools.name: validate_intent
tools.description: READ-ONLY pre-flight for a generate_scene intent table: returns the scene capability report (es-plus.capabilities@1 — which keys are accepted / degraded / unsupported / missing) plus deterministic per-field issues (unknown surfaces, duplicate props, missing formtype, membership flags such as inQuery, labels absent from the spec, system fields inside an editable form, malformed dialog entries). It judges and never repairs or generates. Call it after extracting surfaces from a PRD / wireframe and before generating; fix the errors and re-run.

scene.description: The scene the intent is for — same value you would pass to generate_scene.

intent.description: The scene intent table (scene='crud': name/apiUrl/surfaces…; fragments: fields…). The same object you would pass as generate_scene's `intent`.

spec.description: Optional spec text (PRD / wireframe transcription). When present, every field label must appear verbatim in it — the check catches labels the host paraphrased instead of copying.

tools.name: coverage_report
tools.description: READ-ONLY per-page coverage classification for a structured spec inventory: L1 = generate_scene emits the page faithfully with no post-edit (metadata-only keys such as name/apiUrl/mode may lack a carrier but need no host edit); L2 = it emits, but a behavior-bearing key is degraded, the page composes several fragments, or the host declares extension points; L3 = an intent key is unsupported / required keys are missing / the intent shape is invalid / the host declares code of its own. The verdict comes from the es-plus.capabilities@1 ledger (assessIntent) plus the same front-door Zod shapes, not from prose, so the same inventory always yields the same levels. Run validate_intent first to get per-field detail.

name.description: Page name for the report (defaults to page-<n>).

scene.description: Single-part shorthand: use scene + intent instead of parts[].

intent.description: That scene's intent table (same shape validate_intent checks).

parts.description: When the page is assembled from several generated pieces (multi-table master-detail, form + dialog, …), list them here — they will be composed with generate_composition.

extensionPoints.description: Host-declared extension points on an otherwise generated page (e.g. a toolbar slot or a custom cell). Any entry makes the page L2.

hostCode.description: Host-code items the declarative path cannot emit (charts, bespoke business widgets, custom routing…). Any entry makes the page L3.

items.description: One page of the structured inventory.

pages.description: The structured page inventory (one entry per page of the spec).

tools.name: get_component_api
tools.description: Get the full API documentation for an es-plus component, including TypeScript interfaces, props, methods, and usage examples. Specify target='vue2' for @es-plus/vue2 + Element UI variants, target='antdv' for @es-plus/adapter-antdv + Ant Design Vue; default is target='vue3'.

component.description: Component name: EsForm, EsTable, EsDialog, EsCrudPage, SvgIcon, or useDialog (detailed docs for all six; the EsTable doc also covers the vxe engine)

target.description: Target framework: 'vue3' (default, @es-plus/vue3 + Element Plus), 'vue2' (@es-plus/vue2 + Element UI), or 'antdv' (@es-plus/adapter-antdv + Ant Design Vue, Vue 3 syntax). Match the user's project.

tools.name: scaffold_page
tools.description: Generate a minimal es-plus page scaffold (.vue SFC) — plus the SAME `preflight` checklist that generated CRUD pages emit (httpRequest / permission / t / JSX plugin / UI library), with a copy-once app-entry boilerplate (vue3: `app.use(ESPlus, { permission, t, httpRequest })`, vue2: `Vue.use`). Supports vue3 (default) / vue2 / antdv targets. Use this when you need a blank starting template; use `doctor_page` to check an entry the host already has.

features.description: Features to include. Defaults to ['query', 'table']. Options: query, table, dialog

target.description: Target framework: 'vue3' (default, <script setup> + @es-plus/vue3), 'vue2' (defineComponent + setup() + @es-plus/vue2), or 'antdv' (<script setup> + @es-plus/adapter-antdv + Ant Design Vue)

tools.name: doctor_page
tools.description: Static-check a host app entry against the es-plus preflight checklist (UI library, ESPlus plugin registration, httpRequest, permission, t, JSX transform). Pass the entry source and optionally the config the page was generated from (so only the capabilities that page actually needs are required) plus vite.config source (for UI auto-import / JSX plugin). Literal scan only: results are ok / missing / unverified — unverified means the item may be satisfied elsewhere and must be checked by hand.

entry.description: Source of the app entry, e.g. src/main.ts (or src/main.js for vue2).

target.description: Target framework the entry is for.

config.description: Optional: the StructuredCrudConfig the page was generated from. When given, permission / t / httpRequest / JSX are required only if that config actually uses them.

viteConfig.description: Optional: vite.config.* source. Needed to verify UI-library auto-import and the JSX plugin.

instructions:
# es-plus MCP server

This server exposes the same tool implementations that ship with @es-plus/cli,
giving you typed, schema-validated CRUD code generation for all three Vue render
targets:

  - **@es-plus/vue3** (Vue 3 + Element Plus) — default
  - **@es-plus/vue2** (Vue 2 + Element UI)
  - **@es-plus/adapter-antdv** (Vue 3 + Ant Design Vue)

## Always pick the right target

Every code-generating tool (generate_scene / generate_composition / generate_crud /
generate_crud_from_config / generate_form / generate_table /
generate_dialog / generate_crud_page / generate_crud_schema /
scaffold_page / get_component_api) accepts a `target: 'vue3' | 'vue2' | 'antdv'`
parameter. **Detect the target FIRST**, then call the generator:

1. Read the user's project `package.json` (use your file-read tool)
2. Call `detect_project_target` with the JSON content
3. Pass the returned `target` to every subsequent tool call

If you skip detection, you'll default to vue3 — which silently produces
`<script setup>` / `v-model:*` / Element Plus imports that won't compile in
a Vue 2 project, or the wrong UI-library imports for an Ant Design Vue project.

Note: `antdv` uses Vue 3 syntax (identical to vue3); only the UI-library
symbols differ — `message` / `Modal` / `Tag` from ant-design-vue, and
`<a-tag :color>` instead of `<el-tag :type>`.

## Tool selection — ONE front door, then fill the intent table

Do NOT shop around the tool list. For almost every request, the entry point is
**`generate_scene`**, and your only real decision is `scene` plus filling that
scene's intent table — for a page, `scene: 'crud'` and which of **query / table /
form / dialog** the request implies, and the fields in each. Routing after that
is deterministic code, not your choice:

  - any **table** present → composed and compiled through the single
    golden-covered generator (one-shot compile guaranteed);
  - **no table** (standalone form, a search filter, an add/edit dialog on its
    own, form+dialog) → emitted as self-contained fragments.

So "which tool / how many tools" collapses to "set the surfaces that match the
request". Table-only, query+table, table+add/edit, full CRUD, dialog-only — all
are just different `surfaces` subsets of the SAME `{ scene: 'crud', intent }`
call. **`generate_crud` is the same route under a compatibility name** (identical
bytes) — use it only if a host prompt already names it.

Use a standalone tool ONLY for an explicit single-component ask, or to produce a
fragment you'll drop next to native / third-party components:

  - `generate_form`  — one `<es-form>` SFC (filter / settings / embedded form)
  - `generate_table` — one `<es-table>` SFC (list that sits beside other UI)
  - `generate_dialog`— one `useXxxDialog()` composable (reusable add/edit modal)

When several of those pieces must live TOGETHER in one page (but the request is
not a CRUD page), use **`generate_composition`** — it wires row actions to
dialogs, query/reset to the table, and dialog success to a table refresh.

Never hand-assemble a CRUD page by calling several standalone tools — that
re-introduces the orchestration mistakes the front door exists to prevent. Fill
`surfaces` and let the routing compose them.

(`generate_crud_from_config` remains available if you want to hand-author a full
typed `StructuredCrudConfig` directly — `generate_scene` (scene='crud') and
`generate_crud` are thinner intent layers over the same deterministic
generator. `generate_crud_page` uses a regex NL parser and is only a no-LLM
fallback for hosts that can't reason.)

## Mapping the surfaces (same reasoning as the config path)

**YOU do the reasoning** — read the natural-language request and fill each
surface's fields by understanding intent. This is real semantic mapping, not
keyword matching.

Two passes, every time:

1. **Read first**: `esplus://examples/surfaces` (few-shot NL→`generate_scene`
   (scene='crud') surfaces across every subset — the front-door decision) and/or
   `esplus://examples/nl-to-config` (few-shot NL→full config with reasoning),
   plus `esplus://conventions` + `esplus://types` for the target.
2. **Draft** the surfaces: map each requested field by MEANING, not keywords —
   status/type/enum → Select (dataOptions, or apiParams for remote); date/time →
   DatePicker/TimePicker; image/file → Upload; on/off → Switch; any numeric
   value (amount / price / quantity / stock / count / money / integer) →
   InputNumber. Membership is
   implied by WHICH surface list a field appears in: a filter field goes in
   `surfaces.query`, a visible column in `surfaces.table`, a mutable add/edit
   field in `surfaces.form`. A field that appears in several surfaces is listed
   in each — the generator reconciles duplicates deterministically (identity
   first-wins, semantic from form, display from table). System columns: put in
   `table` but not `form`; detail-only: put in `table`/`form` but not
   `query`. (If you hand-author the full config instead, this is the
   `inQuery`/`inTable`/`inForm` partition.)
3. **Self-review** against the original request BEFORE calling:
   - Did every field the user named make it in, with the right `formtype`?
   - Is each field in the right surface list(s)? Did you set `surfaces.dialog`
     for every add/edit/view the request implies? (A dialog entry is a canned
     key `add`/`edit`/`view`, or a full object `{ key, title?, width?,
     fullscreen?, formItems? }` when the request names a custom dialog id /
     title / width or a per-dialog field list.)
   - Are all requested actions present? Do Select/Cascader fields have options?
   - Business logic the schema can't express (permission gates, conditional
     display, computed values) → emit a typed extension point
     (`permissionValue` / `formatter` / `render`). **Mark it, never drop it.**
4. **Validate before generating** — call `validate_intent` with the same
   `{ scene, intent }` (plus the spec text when you have it). It returns the
   capability report and per-field issues (surface membership, duplicate props,
   missing formtype, labels absent from the spec, system fields in a form).
   Fix every error and re-run; it only judges and never generates. For a
   multi-page spec, `coverage_report` classifies each page from the same ledger:
   L1 direct emit / L2 direct emit + extension points / L3 host code.
5. **Call** `generate_scene` (scene='crud') or its compatibility alias
   `generate_crud`/`generate_crud_from_config`, then **read the
   returned warnings** — each one flags a likely mapping mistake; fix and
   regenerate.
6. **Read the `preflight` section** at the end of the result. It lists the HOST
   prerequisites (`app.use(ESPlus, { httpRequest, permission, t })`, the UI
   library, and — for mode=sfc dialogs — the JSX plugin) with a copy-once entry
   boilerplate. These do not break compilation; the matching capability silently
   turns inert, and a missing `permission` fails OPEN. When the host already has
   an entry, pass it to `doctor_page` and act on every `missing` line.

## Resources

Steering few-shots (target-independent — read before generating):

  - `esplus://examples/surfaces` — NL → `generate_scene` (scene='crud') surfaces, every subset (the front-door decision)
  - `esplus://examples/nl-to-config` — NL → full StructuredCrudConfig, with reasoning
  - `esplus://capabilities` — scene capability ledger (`es-plus.capabilities@1`): accepted/required intent keys per scene, CRUD key dispositions per mode (downgrade + reason), target × key matrix. Read it before composing an intent to know which keys actually land in the artifact.

The remaining resource URIs use a target suffix:

  - `esplus://conventions` (vue3 default) / `esplus://conventions/vue2` / `esplus://conventions/antdv`
  - `esplus://examples` (vue3 default) / `esplus://examples/vue2` / `esplus://examples/antdv`
  - `esplus://types` (vue3 default) / `esplus://types/vue2` / `esplus://types/antdv`
  - `esplus://crud-page-schema` (vue3 default) / `esplus://crud-page-schema/vue2` / `esplus://crud-page-schema/antdv`

Fetch the vue2 / antdv variants when working in those codebases — the JSON
config shapes are identical, but syntax examples (defineComponent + setup,
.sync, element-ui imports for vue2; ant-design-vue imports for antdv) differ.

## Schema is portable

The defining feature of es-plus is that `formItemList`, `columns`,
`options`, and `CrudPageSchema` JSON are byte-identical across vue2, vue3,
and antdv. Only the wrapper SFC syntax / UI-library symbols change. When
refining an existing schema across turns, you can keep the same JSON and just
regenerate.
